title: 약을 먹고도 안 나아요: -고도 / -거니와
objective: By the end, you can use -고도 to say that a result goes against what you expected, and -거니와 to add a second point that goes the same way as the first.
summary: This worksheet compares -고도 ("even after doing") and -거니와 ("not only… but also") so you can use each one correctly.

task.title: Choose, fill in, and write
task.line: Decide whether the sentence needs an unexpected result (-고도) or an added point (-거니와), then write the correct form.

forms.when: After an action verb, with or without a final consonant. Do not put -았/었- before it. Show past tense at the end of the sentence.
forms.means: Even after doing A, B happens. B goes against what you expect (like 그런데도).
forms.exampleMeaning: Even after taking medicine, my cold didn't get better.

forms.when: Often used with verbs of knowing or seeing, to complain that someone acted as if they didn't know or see.
forms.means: Someone knew, saw, or read something but still didn't act on it.
forms.example: 동생은 제 문자를 읽고도 답장을 안 해요.
forms.exampleMeaning: My younger sibling reads my texts but still doesn't reply.

forms.when: After verbs and adjectives, often in the pattern A도 -거니와 B도. Mostly used in writing and formal speech.
forms.means: Not only A, but also B (like 뿐만 아니라). A and B point the same way, both good or both bad.
forms.example: 이 동네는 교통도 편리하거니와 공원도 많아요.
forms.exampleMeaning: This neighborhood not only has convenient transportation, but also has many parks.

forms.when: Unlike -고도, -거니와 can take the past tense -았/었-.
forms.means: Not only did A happen, B also happened.
forms.example: 어제는 잠도 못 잤거니와 아침도 못 먹었어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: Yesterday I not only couldn't sleep, I also couldn't eat breakfast.

forms.means: Not only is someone or something N, it is also B.
forms.example: 그 사람은 제 동료이거니와 오랜 친구이기도 해요.
forms.exampleMeaning: He's not only my coworker, he's also an old friend.

watchOut: 밥을 먹었고도 (X) → 밥을 먹고도 (O): Never put -았/었- before -고도. Show the time at the end of the sentence.
비싸거니와 맛있어요 (X) → 비싸지만 맛있어요 (O): -거니와 adds a point that goes the same way. For a contrast, use -지만.
피곤하고도 일했어요 (X) → 피곤한데도 일했어요 (O): In this meaning, use -고도 after action verbs. After adjectives, use -(으)ㄴ데도.
exercises: Choose the right form: ① 그 친구는 약속 시간을 (알고도 / 알거니와) 또 늦었어요. ② 이 노트북은 무게도 (가볍고도 / 가볍거니와) 배터리도 오래가요. ③ 이 방은 (좁거니와 / 좁지만) 깨끗해요.
Fill in the blank with 듣다 + -고도: 선생님 설명을 두 번이나 ____ 이해를 못 했어요.
Fill in the blank with 오다 + -거니와 (past): 어제는 비도 많이 ____ 바람도 세게 불었어요.
Correct the error and rewrite the sentence: 지도를 봤고도 길을 잃었어요.
Combine the two sentences into one with -거니와: 이 일은 시간이 많이 걸려요. 돈도 많이 들어요.
Answer in Korean with -고도. Your friend asks: 아까 왜 저를 보고 그냥 지나갔어요? (You saw your friend but did not recognize them.)
answers: ① 알고도 ② 가볍거니와 ③ 좁지만
이 일은 시간도 많이 걸리거니와 돈도 많이 들어요. (이 일은 시간이 많이 걸리거니와 돈도 많이 들어요.)
미안해요. 보고도 못 알아봤어요. (죄송해요. 보고도 몰라봤어요.)
